correctness.rationale: With Euclidean distances, two points from different axes have squared distance w_i+w_j irrespective of signs and each antipodal pair squared distance 4w_i. Thus the Rips flag complex is the graph T_t fiber substitution by S^0 when t<4w_i or simplex Δ^1 when t≥4w_i. Every nonempty active weighted-threshold subgraph has a universal minimum-weight vertex: if jk is an edge then both w_v+w_j and w_v+w_k are ≤w_j+w_k. For t<4w_1 all fibers are S^0, the active complex is S^0*J(T\{v})=ΣJ, while s isolated axes are 2s isolated vertices. This gives exact terminating F(I;z)=2s+z F(A\{v};z), base 2|I|-1, and integral sphere wedges by induction. For t≥4w_1, if an active edge exists axis 1 is active/universal and its filled antipodal edge joins the active complex, making that component contractible; remaining isolated fibers contribute 1 or 2 contractible components as in c formula. If no active edges all fibers are isolated and c formula still works. Equality thresholds, positive weights, all d≥2, repeated lengths and mixed-degree intervals are included; no persistence maps claimed. An independent evaluation for w=(100,113,212,218), t=325 gives active edges 12,13,14,23 and F=z²+2z. Frozen VERIFY.py constructs exact clique complexes and boundary ranks modulo 2 across 570 stages; the universal integer statement follows from join homotopy, not mod-two data.
